original_value: As outlined in the 3Gpp Release 16, 5G satellite access is important for 5G network development in the future. A terrestrial-satellite network integrated with 5G has the characteristics of low delay, high bandwidth, and ubiquitous coverage. A few researchers have proposed integrated schemes for such a network; however, these schemes do not consider the possibility of achieving optimization of the delay characteristic by changing the computing mode of the 5G satellite network. We propose a 5G satellite edge computing framework (5GsatEC), which aims to reduce delay and expand network coverage. This framework consists of embedded hardware platforms and edge computing microservices in satellites. To increase the flexibility of the framework in complex scenarios, we unify the resource management of the central processing unit (CPU), graphics processing unit (GPU), and field-programmable gate array (FPGA); we divide the services into three types: system services, basic services, and user services. In order to verify the performance of the framework, we carried out a series of experiments. The results show that 5GsatEC has a broader coverage than the ground 5G network. The results also show that 5GsatEC has lower delay, a lower packet loss rate, and lower bandwidth consumption than the 5G satellite network.

result.paraphrase: According to 3Gpp Release 16, 5G satellite access will play an important role in the future development of 5G networks. A 5G-integrated terrestrial-satellite network is characterized by low latency, high bandwidth, and ubiquitous coverage. Although several researchers have proposed integrated schemes for this kind of network, they do not address the possibility of optimizing delay by changing the computing mode of the 5G satellite network. We present a 5G satellite edge computing framework (5GsatEC) designed to reduce delay and extend network coverage. The framework includes embedded hardware platforms and edge-computing microservices on satellites. To improve flexibility in complex scenarios, we unify resource management for the central processing unit (CPU), graphics processing unit (GPU), and field-programmable gate array (FPGA), and classify services into system services, basic services, and user services. To evaluate the framework, we conducted a series of experiments. The results indicate that 5GsatEC provides broader coverage than the ground 5G network, and also achieves lower delay, a lower packet loss rate, and lower bandwidth consumption than the 5G satellite network.
